preamble: Monophthongization of the falling diphthong ui to i, the rounded back nucleus being absorbed into the front offglide. It is a core development in Japonic: Proto-Japonic *ui yields i in Proto-Ryukyuan and the vowel i₂ in Old Japanese (later merged with i), producing alternations such as Old Japanese tuki₂ 'moon' beside bound tuku-.

examples.to: tuki₂ (bound form tuku-, as in tukuyo 'moonlit night'); Modern Japanese tsuki
examples.note: Pre-Old Japanese *ui became the vowel i₂, which merged with i by Early Middle Japanese; the bound form preserves the original u.

examples.to: kami₂ (bound form kamu-); Modern Japanese kami

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Proto-Japonic language (vowel-sequence correspondences: *ui > Old Japanese i₂, Proto-Ryukyuan *i). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Japonic_language
